records.title: Fixed simulation clock
records.meaning: The simulation advances in fixed increments; rendering follows the display clock. State S contains bodies, timers, health, inventory and encounters. A repeatable step size makes cooldown and contact semantics inspectable, but it does not make an unseeded random simulation reproducible.
records.composition: Input is sampled before movement; collision, attacks, healing, projectiles, loot and persistence follow in source order. Changing that order changes outcomes.
records.boundary: Floating-point arithmetic, iteration order and Math.random remain sources of divergence. Fixed step is not a claim of cross-platform lockstep.

records.title: Accumulator overload policy
records.meaning: Elapsed wall time enters an accumulator. At most four fixed updates execute per display callback; excess accumulation is discarded under the existing guard. This deliberately prioritizes responsiveness over catching up after a stall.
records.composition: All simulation timers share the resulting game clock, so overload slows gameplay relative to wall time rather than selectively skipping enemy cooldowns.
records.boundary: The elapsed cap is 80 milliseconds; four steps cover about 66.7 milliseconds. The policy can lose time and is not real-time conservation.

records.title: Directional ellipse support
records.meaning: The support function gives the farthest projection of an ellipse onto a unit direction. It is used in separation estimates. It differs from the radius of the ellipse along a ray; substituting the latter underestimates diagonal support.
records.composition: Rotate the world normal into the ellipse frame, normalize it, evaluate support, and combine two supports for a separation target.
records.boundary: This support-based center-direction response is not a complete exact ellipse-ellipse intersection solver or rigid-body impulse calculation.

records.title: Exact ellipse-circle contact
records.meaning: For an exterior point p in ellipse coordinates, a nonnegative Lagrange multiplier t determines the closest ellipse point. Eighteen bisection iterations approximate the root. Contact is accepted when the resulting distance is smaller than the circle radius.
records.composition: An enclosing-radius rejection runs first, followed by an interior test, then root solving only for surviving candidates.
records.boundary: Tangency uses strict comparisons and finite precision. Very thin or degenerate axes would require additional guards outside current creature definitions.

records.title: Ten-strike durability exchange
records.equation: strikes = 10 if ordinary and H_petal > D_mob; else 1
records.meaning: An overlapping ordinary petal may perform up to ten exchange iterations in a single fixed update. The loop stops when the petal breaks or the monster dies. This rule is evaluated every tick; it is not a ten-hits-per-second cap.
records.composition: Durability declines between strikes, so later raw damage in the same batch is weaker. Armor is also evaluated separately for each strike.
records.boundary: The theoretical loop ceiling is 600 strikes per second per sustained pair before durability and death constraints. Actual contact uptime is much smaller and state-dependent.
records.verification: Construct high-durability targets and log strikes per tick, durability decline and death truncation. Benchmark before changing this balance-sensitive rule.

records.title: Inventory-constrained greedy build
records.equation: n[k]=bag[k]+count_current(k); maximize sum_k x[k]*s[k] subject to 0<=x[k]<=n[k], sum_k x[k]=N
records.meaning: Sort by descending per-copy additive score, then ascending ASCII item key; take the available copies until N slots are filled. The exchange argument proves optimality for this additive model: replacing any selected lower score by an available higher score cannot decrease the objective.
records.composition: The backup deck is excluded from the pool. Exactly N current slots are filled, N in 1..10. No RNG is consumed by planning.
records.boundary: An optimum of this preference model need not win a battle. Equal-score selection is deterministic and may rearrange the current deck.
